generator.params.bud_area.note: The leaf area its `bud` look draws on an organ 1 m long (plantc's shading-area test), so it shades with what it shows: the bud is now its flower closed, where before it drew the fruit ovoid.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Jepson 1925, Dicentra formosa, Fig. 404, p. 405: naked scape-like flowering stems 8 in to 18 in high, a little taller than the leaves (Abrams vol. 2, p. 234, gives the basal leaves as 3 dm to 5 dm long but no scape height).

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a delicate herb with lacy, fern-like, blue-green leaves and arching stems hung with pink, heart-shaped flowers. Each stalk ends in one nodding raceme drawn as a cluster (flowers 1, flower_size 0.1 within the 5 cm to 15 cm the species states; its look's inflorescence 8 flowers, each a fifth of its length, bent 60 degrees), now that Papaveraceae's flowers are mostly in racemes; before, the stalk bore 8 single flowers. leaf_area 0.193 is what its lobed leaf card draws on an organ 1 m long since the lobed card takes its lobes, depth and width from the traits (nightshades round 5; re-measured with plantc atlas on the poppies' dissected leaves when the two merged). Its basal leaves (poppies, 2026-10-19) 40 cm long with their stalks, so the blades come out about 17-26 cm, inside Flora of North America's (15-)25-40 cm while the plant stays under Jepson's 18 in scapes; rising 30 degrees from upright and turned 0.3 of the way flat, so the blades are held level over the stalks as a low mound. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 0.4 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: grey blue-green leaves (Flora of North America vol. 3, Dicentra formosa, read on eFloras 2026-10-19: abaxial and sometimes adaxial surface glaucous); pink flowers. The basal leaf card (poppies, 2026-10-19): a ternate blade (FNA: blade with 3-5 orders of leaflets and lobes), its three divisions each pinnate, 7 pinnules of 5 segments, joined at their bases into a dissected blade (confluent 0.6) with oblong lobes (FNA: penultimate lobes oblong, 10-20 x 3-4 mm), on a petiole a third its length. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): four pink petals by hand (in two pairs; the drawing has no joined heart-shaped corolla) above two sepals, six stamens and a pistil of two carpels, from the characters of Papaveraceae and Dicentra by the rules at the flowering plants.

generator.params.bud_spacing.note: The flowers hang in a short cluster at the top of the nodding stalk, and the buds at its tip about half as far apart as the open flowers by eye (flowering photographs, observations 78668413, 156536515, 159323269, 396852962, 171777385, 27542805, 165256931, 217405336): a bud's internode as a share of a flower's, judged by eye.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Flora of North America vol. 3, Fumariaceae, Dicentra formosa (efloras.org, read 2026-10-19), family: flowers bilaterally symmetric about each of 2 perpendicular planes; outer petals both swollen or spurred basally; corolla cordate to oblong in outline.

traits.flower_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 3, Fumariaceae, Dicentra formosa (efloras.org, read 2026-10-19): petals rose-purple, pink, cream, or pale yellow, rarely white (subsp. formosa rose-purple to pink); the pink is our reading of the iNaturalist photos (batch poppies-2026-10-19).

traits.flower_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3, Fumariaceae, Dicentra formosa (efloras.org, read 2026-10-19): outer petals (12-)16-19(-24) mm long, inner petals (12-)15-18(-22) mm; the pendent flower is as long as its outer petals.
